result:
I moved the role comparison out of the feature code, so the new filter no longer compares `user.role` itself. I did not run tests, lint, or the app, as you asked.

The violation was in `apps/react-vite/src/features/users/utils/filter-users.ts`, which had `user.role !== role`. I changed it to call a new helper, `matchesRole(user, role)`, which I added to `apps/react-vite/src/lib/authorization.tsx`. The helper returns true for `'ALL'` or when the user's role equals the filter value. The role comparison now lives in the authorization module, where the existing `POLICIES` already compare roles.

The `users-csv.ts` file also references `user.role`, but it only writes the value into the CSV, so I left it alone.

Two things to check:
- `matchesRole` is a new export from `lib/authorization`, which goes slightly beyond "route it through `Authorization` or `checkAccess`". Those two only cover access checks against the current user, and this is a row filter, so I did not force it through them. If you want the rule applied literally, the alternative is to drop the role filter or move it into the API request.
- I did not type-check the `'ALL' | ROLES` comparison against `User['role']`. It should compile, but `tsc` would confirm it.

Nothing is committed.
